answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation.. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consider a zephyr as the anchor of the cost.
